speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you describe exactly where in your neck and arms you are feeling pain, weakness, or tingling? Also, did these symptoms start suddenly after an injury or have they developed gradually over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the pain or weakness follow a specific pattern, such as being worse on one side or affecting specific fingers, and have you noticed any changes in your bowel or bladder function? REQUEST TEST: Cervical MRI

text: RESULTS: MRI of the cervical spine reveals a syrinx (cavity) within the spinal cord extending from the cervical to the upper thoracic region.

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI findings of a syrinx explain your symptoms, likely secondary to your prior trauma. Do you have any difficulty with fine motor skills like buttoning shirts, or have you noticed any changes in your temperature sensation in your arms?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the combination of a syrinx, absent reflexes, and fasciculations, I suspect involvement of both upper and lower motor neurons. REQUEST TEST: Cervical CT Myelogram

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal CT myelogram rules out compressive lesions, confirming the syrinx is likely non-compressive or related to prior trauma. Do you have any history of Chiari malformation, or have you noticed any sensory loss to pain and temperature specifically while retaining touch sensation?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, hypertension, history of a motor vehicle accident 3 years prior. Social history: 7 sexual partners, uses condoms inconsistently.

speaker: Doctor
text: The history of inconsistent condom use with multiple partners raises concern for neurosyphilis, which can mimic these symptoms. REQUEST TEST: VDRL and CSF analysis for syphilis

speaker: Doctor
text: With syphilis ruled out and the MRI confirming a syrinx, your symptoms of pain/temperature dissociation and hand weakness are classic for Syringomyelia. DIAGNOSIS READY: Syringomyelia
